events.headline: Ferry carrying nearly 270 people capsizes and sinks off northern Cyprus, killing several, dozens missing
events.summary: The passenger ferry Filo Jet, carrying 259 passengers and 8 crew, capsized in rough weather roughly 15 minutes after departing Kyrenia (Girne) for Taşucu, Turkey, on August 30, 2026. At least 7-8 people were confirmed dead, around 24 remained missing, and 237 were rescued; the captain and crew were detained pending investigation.

events.headline: US forces strike Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island; IRGC vows retaliation
events.summary: US CENTCOM struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, August 30, 2026, after observing IRGC forces preparing to fire rockets fitted with sea mines into the strait. Iranian state media reported casualties (unconfirmed toll) and the IRGC vowed "retribution."

events.headline: DR Congo begins Ebola vaccination campaign as world's deadliest outbreak on record deepens
events.summary: DRC's health minister launched an ERVEBO vaccination campaign for frontline workers in Kisangani on August 27, 2026, using compassionate-use protocol since the outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain. As of August 26, 2026, the outbreak had 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths (48% case fatality rate) — the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record.

events.headline: Death toll from Nepal-Tibet border flash flood surpasses 669, thousands still missing
events.summary: A glacier collapse near Langtang Lirung triggered flash floods and mudslides along the Trishuli/Bhotekoshi river system on Aug 26, 2026, devastating multiple districts in Nepal and the Gyirong border crossing into Tibet. As of Aug 29, Nepal reported 669 dead and 2,362 missing (including ~499 foreign nationals), with Tibet reporting additional dead and hundreds missing.

events.headline: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Continues to Climb as Recovery Continues in Chocó
events.summary: The magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck near San José del Palmar, Chocó on August 10, 2026, has an evolving death toll — PAHO's August 14 situation report recorded 287 deaths, 378 missing, and over 13,000 homes destroyed (79,108 damaged) across 15 departments. The Colombian government declared a state of national disaster and deployed troops amid nearly 100 aftershocks.
events.locationName: San José del Palmar, Chocó, Colombia

events.headline: Gunmen kill dozens, kidnap scores in mass attack on four Borgu villages, Niger State
events.summary: Gunmen attacked four communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State on August 21, 2026, abducting worshippers from mosques and residents from homes; scores were killed and abducted. President Tinubu ordered a security manhunt; as of late August the government reported ongoing efforts to secure victims' release.
events.locationName: Borgu Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria

events.headline: Heavy flooding in Tawila, North Darfur destroys homes, displaces families amid worsening crisis
events.summary: Heavy rainfall in the week before August 19, 2026 destroyed or damaged nearly 1,350 homes in Tawila, North Darfur, displacing over 1,000 families. Tawila hosts more than 700,000 displaced people who fled violence in El Fasher; flooding has compounded disease outbreaks in overcrowded camps.

events.headline: Trump Administration Announces "Public-Private Partnership" Giving US Equity Stake in Venezuelan Oil Fields
events.summary: The Trump administration announced a deal securing majority US control (55% JV share) of 17 strategic Venezuelan oil fields holding roughly 65 billion barrels of proven reserves (~21% of Venezuela's total), with the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital holding a 35% non-voting stake in North American Blue Energy Partners. Venezuelan Vice President/acting leader Delcy Rodríguez said the deal, involving over $100 billion in investment, would generate $209 billion in added tax revenue for Venezuela over its term.

events.headline: Two Killed, Nine Wounded in Overnight Trenton, New Jersey Shooting at Large Gathering
events.summary: Gunmen opened fire on an unauthorized gathering of roughly 200 people on the 100 block of Locust Street in Trenton around 12:25 a.m. Sunday, killing two and wounding nine; more than 50 shell casings were recovered at the scene.
events.locationName: Locust Street, Trenton, New Jersey, US

events.headline: Israeli settlers and soldiers attack West Bank village of Al-Mughayyir, four wounded
events.summary: Israeli settlers raided the village of Al-Mughayyir northeast of Ramallah on August 30, 2026, attacking residents and vehicles; accompanying Israeli soldiers then fired live ammunition and tear gas at Palestinians, wounding four. Israeli forces sealed the village's only entrance for more than 20 hours.

events.headline: Measles Outbreaks Surge to Highest Levels in Decades Across the Americas, Threatening US and Mexico Elimination Status
events.summary: PAHO reports the Americas region lost its measles-elimination-free status in November 2025 after endemic transmission was reestablished in Canada. As of August 20, 2026, the CDC reported 2,777 confirmed US measles cases across 36 outbreaks — the highest US total since 1991 — with the US measles-elimination status review scheduled for November 2026 and Mexico also at risk.

events.headline: Woman killed, five injured in shooting at techno rave in Aarau, Switzerland
events.summary: A 22-year-old woman died and five people were injured after shots were fired around 2:30 a.m. at the Schachen racecourse during the "Aargau Rave," attended by roughly 3,500 people. Police launched a manhunt for one or more suspects; authorities have not ruled out terrorism as a motive.

events.headline: One Killed, Nine Wounded in Mass Shooting at Chicago's Washington Park
events.summary: Gunfire erupted into a large late-night gathering in Washington Park on Chicago's South Side around 11:37 p.m. Saturday, striking 10 people; a 35-year-old man later died at University of Chicago Medical Center. Police recovered shell casings from multiple firearm types, including rifle rounds.

events.headline: Xi Jinping's military purge ousts top loyalists Zhang Youxia and Zhong Shaojun from China's legislature
events.summary: China's National People's Congress removed several senior officials from their lawmaker positions, announced Aug 28, 2026. The move leaves the Central Military Commission functionally reduced to Xi and one other member, extending a purge that has swept up 100+ senior PLA officers since 2022-23.

events.headline: Haiti Postpones August 30 General Election to December 13 Amid Gang Violence
events.summary: Haiti's electoral council (CEP), backed by acting PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, postponed the country's first presidential/legislative elections in a decade — originally set for August 30 — to December 13, 2026, with a runoff planned for late February, citing an insufficient security environment. The decision follows continued gang warfare from the Viv Ansanm coalition, including an attack in Kenscoff, and displacement of over a million people nationwide.

events.headline: 2026 wildfire season among the worst on record for Spain and France; over 300,000 evacuated
events.summary: Wildfires across Spain and France in July-August 2026 forced roughly 330,000 people to evacuate, including a peacetime-record evacuation of ~197,000 people near Bordeaux, France. Fires around Madrid, Ávila and Toledo merged into the worst blaze in Madrid region history; French officials described nearly 98,000 hectares burned as a "historic record."

events.headline: Israeli strike destroys Gaza aid warehouse, kills seven amid ongoing ceasefire violations
events.summary: An Israeli strike hit a warehouse holding humanitarian supplies along with a water desalination plant and a mosque in Gaza around August 24-25, 2026, killing at least seven people. The strikes are part of a pattern of violations of the ceasefire in effect since October 2025.

events.headline: Typhoon Saudel makes double landfall in Zhejiang, China, forcing evacuation of over 800,000
events.summary: Typhoon Saudel made its first landfall near Yuhuan, Taizhou, Zhejiang around 8:05am local time on Aug 28, 2026, then a second landfall at Wenzhou. Wenzhou ordered evacuation of over 820,000 people, Taizhou relocated 500,000+; ports and flights across the region were disrupted.

events.headline: Iceland rejects reopening EU accession talks in close referendum
events.summary: Icelanders voted 52.8% to 47.2% against reopening negotiations to join the European Union, with turnout of 82.5%. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir said her government would honor the result and not revisit the issue during her current mandate.

events.headline: Remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly Bring Heavy Rain, Flash Flood Risk to Leeward Islands
events.summary: Dolly weakened to an open tropical wave/post-tropical remnant by Friday, August 28, but its moisture plume was forecast to move into the Leeward Islands overnight Saturday into Sunday, bringing heavy rain and flash flood risk. The remnant moisture was also expected to affect the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, and Haiti into Monday.

events.headline: Two Frankfurt Airport workers die after contracting "airport malaria"
events.summary: Six employees at Frankfurt Airport contracted malaria believed transmitted by an Anopheles mosquito that arrived on an incoming flight; two of the six died, with the death toll reaching two by August 27, 2026. Germany's Robert Koch Institute is investigating the mosquito's origin.

events.headline: Argentina's Economic Recovery Loses Momentum as Milei Faces 2027 Election Headwinds
events.summary: Economists cut Argentina's 2026 growth forecast to 2.7%; mass consumption fell 3.7% year-on-year in Q2 2026. Inflation is expected to end 2026 near 29-30%, and President Javier Milei's approval rating has slipped to around 37%, complicating his path to reelection in 2027.

events.headline: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse; 50% US Tariffs and Canadian Retaliation Take Effect
events.summary: US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed the night of August 21-22, 2026, just before 50% US tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods took effect. PM Mark Carney blamed "unfair" US demands; Canada announced retaliatory tariffs effective September 8.

events.headline: US Treasury intensifies Iran sanctions campaign, plans new bank designation
events.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled a sweeping new sanctions campaign against Iran in late August 2026, targeting shipping, oil, crypto, gold and aviation sectors, and announced plans to sanction another bank. Bessent said President Trump is personally calling world leaders to press for coordinated economic isolation of Iran.

events.headline: Taiwan confirms first two locally-acquired mpox clade Ib cases
events.summary: Taiwan's CDC confirmed two locally-acquired mpox clade Ib infections around Aug 26, 2026 — the first local transmission of this clade in Taiwan. Nine total clade Ib cases have been recorded since May 2026 (7 imported, 2 local).

events.headline: Kim Yo Jong warns of "counteraction" as US, South Korea, Japan plan trilateral drill
events.summary: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong criticized planned US-South Korea-Japan trilateral nuclear/missile-defense exercise set for Sept 9-11, 2026, accusing Japan of building preemptive-strike capability. North Korea had conducted several ballistic missile tests earlier in August (Aug 6, 11-12, and ~10 short-range missiles around Aug 20).

events.headline: Uganda's military chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba declares bid for 2031 presidency
events.summary: General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces and son of President Yoweri Museveni, announced via X on August 25, 2026 that he will run for president in 2031, saying he expects to win 90% of the vote with his father's backing.

events.headline: Tadej Pogačar suffers concussion, broken collarbone and neck fracture in Vuelta a España crash
events.summary: Race leader Tadej Pogačar crashed with roughly 32-33 km remaining in stage 8 of the Vuelta a España on August 29, 2026, and abandoned the race. His team confirmed a concussion, a displaced fracture of the left collarbone, and a stable C7 cervical fracture; he was transferred to a hospital in Barcelona.

events.headline: Chinese stocks slip as US threatens tariffs, sanctions on banks over Iran ties
events.summary: The Shanghai Composite fell 0.11% to 3,952.2 and the Shenzhen Component dropped 0.68% on Aug 28, 2026, as investors grew cautious over reports of a possible 7.5% US tariff on Chinese goods and Treasury warnings on Chinese banks facilitating Iran-linked transactions.

events.headline: Protesters clash with police outside Indonesian parliament demanding corruption asset-forfeiture bill
events.summary: Groups rallied at the Senayan parliamentary complex in Jakarta on Aug 27, 2026, demanding passage of the Asset Forfeiture Bill. Police deployed roughly 18,500 officers, used water cannon and tear gas after nightfall clashes, and detained dozens.

events.headline: Malian musician Salif Keïta cancels South Africa Macufe Festival show over xenophobic violence
events.summary: Malian Afro-pop star Salif Keïta announced he is cancelling his planned September 12, 2026 performance at South Africa's Macufe festival in Bloemfontein, citing reports of xenophobic violence against African migrants, amid nationwide anti-migrant protests in South Africa.

events.headline: Pakistan's human rights body faults "disproportionate" force against PoK protesters, questions election credibility
events.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, in a report released around Aug 29-30, 2026, said state security forces used disproportionate force against protesters in Pakistan-administered Kashmir and raised concerns about election credibility amid allegations of rigging.

events.headline: Uganda's Toro Kingdom "Boy King" Oyo dies at 34
events.summary: Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, monarch of the Toro Kingdom in western Uganda who was crowned at age 3 in 1995, died on August 27, 2026 while receiving medical treatment in the United States. Toro Kingdom's prime minister confirmed the death.

events.headline: Measles outbreak linked to Swedish music festival grows to 35 cases
events.summary: A measles outbreak traced to the Ukult (Urkult) festival held July 30-August 2, 2026, had grown to 35 confirmed cases across nine Swedish regions by August 27, mostly among unvaccinated children and adolescents. Stockholm and other regions began offering free measles vaccination in response.

events.headline: Pacific Islands Forum leadership presses US, World Bank and UN for Pacific Resilience Facility funding
events.summary: The Pacific Islands Forum chair and secretary-general met UN Secretary-General António Guterres in the week of Aug 20-26, 2026, seeking support to close the funding gap for the Pacific Resilience Facility, a $500 million climate adaptation fund that has raised only about $116-137 million to date.
